intent: To illustrate the changing trends in civil war resolutions, highlighting a shift from military victory to diplomatic negotiation over time.

units.meaning: Military victory as a share of civil-war endings declined from 44.4% until 1989 to 15.6% currently.

basis.note: row bar_100 until-1989, value=1.000, relative_value=0.4444; color #E67E22 inferred as victory from narration
row bar_100 currently, value=0.350, relative_value=0.1556; color #A0522D inferred as victory

accepted_routes: Victory share dropped by about 29 percentage points, from 44% to 16%.
Military victory became much rarer, falling by roughly 65% relative to its 1989 share.
Victories declined from about 44% of endings to about 16%.
units.visual_evidence_rule: Victory-series bars for both periods must be visible, with labels or axis positions showing 44.4% and 15.6% (or heights proportional).
units.temporal_anchor: Victory for one side in a civil war was common, while nowadays, victories are much rarer.
units.reviewer_question: Should the video be required to state the military-victory decline from 44.4% to 15.6%, or is showing the downward trend sufficient?

units.meaning: Negotiated endings as a share of civil-war endings increased from 11.1% until 1989 to 44.4% currently.

basis.note: row bar_100 until-1989, value=0.250, relative_value=0.1111; color #1F3A5F inferred as negotiated from narration
row bar_100 currently, value=1.000, relative_value=0.4444; color #5B9BD5 inferred as negotiated

units.computation: 0.4444 - 0.1111 = 0.3333 (+33.3 percentage points); relative change ((0.4444-0.1111)/0.1111) = 3.0 = 300%, i.e. roughly quadrupled
accepted_routes: Negotiated settlements jumped by about 33 percentage points, from 11% to 44%.
Negotiated endings roughly quadrupled, from about one-tenth to over two-fifths of endings.
Diplomatic negotiation grew from 11.1% until 1989 to 44.4% currently.
units.visual_evidence_rule: Negotiation-series bars for both periods must be visible, with labels or axis positions showing 11.1% and 44.4%.
units.temporal_anchor: At the same time, negotiated endings have jumped...
units.reviewer_question: Should the negotiated-ending increase from 11.1% to 44.4% be required as a separate unit?

units.meaning: The leading resolution type reversed: until 1989 military victory exceeded negotiated endings (44.4% vs 11.1%), but currently negotiated endings exceed military victory (44.4% vs 15.6%).

basis.note: row bar_100 until-1989, relative_value=0.4444; inferred as victory
row bar_100 until-1989, relative_value=0.1111; inferred as negotiated
row bar_100 currently, relative_value=0.1556; inferred as victory
row bar_100 currently, relative_value=0.4444; inferred as negotiated

accepted_routes: Victory led negotiation 44.4% to 11.1% until 1989, but negotiation led victory 44.4% to 15.6% currently.
Military victory was ahead in the earlier period; negotiated endings are ahead now.
There was a crossover from victory-dominant to negotiation-dominant endings.
Negotiated endings overtook military victories as the larger share.
units.visual_evidence_rule: Both resolution series across both periods must be visible together so the viewer can see the order reversal/crossover; labels or legend must distinguish victory from negotiation.
units.temporal_anchor: The contrast between 'Victory... was common' and 'At the same time, negotiated endings have jumped...'
units.reviewer_question: Is the crossover/order reversal required, or are the two separate trend statements sufficient?

units.meaning: Currently, negotiated endings are the largest shown resolution share at 44.4%, versus military victory at 15.6%.

basis.note: row bar_100 currently, relative_value=0.4444; inferred as negotiated
row bar_100 currently, relative_value=0.1556; inferred as victory

units.computation: 0.4444 / 0.1556 = 2.856, so negotiation is about 2.9 times victory; difference 0.4444 - 0.1556 = 0.2888 (28.9 pp).
accepted_routes: Currently, negotiated endings are the largest shown outcome at 44.4%, versus 15.6% for military victory.
Today negotiation leads the categories shown, at 44.4%, nearly three times the 15.6% victory share.
In the current period, negotiated endings are more common than military victories by a 44.4% to 15.6% margin.
units.visual_evidence_rule: Current-period negotiation bar must be visibly taller than the current-period victory bar, with numeric labels or axis positions for 44.4% and 15.6%.
units.reviewer_question: Should the current negotiation-leading value be required beyond the reversal unit?

units.meaning: Until 1989, military victory was the largest shown resolution share at 44.4%, about four times negotiated endings at 11.1%.

basis.note: row bar_100 until-1989, relative_value=0.4444; inferred as victory
row bar_100 until-1989, relative_value=0.1111; inferred as negotiated

accepted_routes: Until 1989, military victory was the largest shown outcome at 44.4%, four times the 11.1% negotiated share.
In the earlier period, victories outnumbered negotiated endings 44.4% to 11.1%.
Before 1989, victory was roughly four times as common as negotiation.
units.visual_evidence_rule: Until-1989 victory bar must be visibly taller than the until-1989 negotiation bar, with numeric labels or axis positions for 44.4% and 11.1%.
units.temporal_anchor: Victory for one side in a civil war was common
units.reviewer_question: Should the earlier victory-leading value be required beyond the reversal unit?

optional_valid: Mention that the current negotiated share is about 44% (rounded from 44.4%) rather than the narration's 'almost 40%'.
Mention the relative decline of military victory by about 65% using (0.1556-0.4444)/0.4444.
Use color/legend to distinguish military victory from negotiated endings.
Show both periods on a common axis for comparison.
unsupported_to_avoid: Causal claims that diplomacy caused the decline in military victories.
Extrapolating the trend beyond the UNTIL 1989 and CURRENTLY periods.
Claiming the two shown categories sum to 100% of all civil-war endings.
Using the narration's 10% or 'almost 40%' as exact values when the table gives 11.1% and 44.4%.
Inventing values for other resolution types or other years.
notes: Values cited use relative_value; colors are used only to link table rows to the victory/negotiation series inferred from the narration. The core required content is the two directional changes plus the reversal/crossover.
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only
